title: Sudden phase resets fit released TESS CPV sector shifts as well as continuous diffusion
abstract: We test whether loss of relative phase memory in complex periodic variables requires a continuous random walk. We fit full circular phase densities to 1,289 released TESS sector pairs from 65 stars. Diffusion, sudden jumps to a new uniform phase, and a model with both use equal total weight per star. Five-fold validation keeps all pairs of a star together. The reset-minus-diffusion mean log loss is -0.075, with a 95% star bootstrap interval of -0.176 to 0.029. Lower loss is better. Both stricter shape cuts and all pairs give intervals that include zero. A cut that removes reused sectors retains the reset fit. Equal pair weights instead favour diffusion, so the comparison depends on the sampling target. Four further fold partitions give the same small score preference. Numerical density checks and 20 synthetic recovery trials confirm that the tested model families are distinct. The main reset fit has a phase width of 0.0179 cycles and a mean reset interval of 401 days; these are descriptive model values. The data permit resets without continuous diffusion. They do not select resets over diffusion or measure material life. Template errors, changing spot patterns, dependent pairs, selected stars and untested heterogeneous models limit physical inference. Code, aggregate evidence, exact input hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are supplied. External stellar records are not bundled.
